author: Marcus R. Brown
description:
`apps/moo-dang/src/utils/performance-optimizations.ts` has no consumers. 571 lines exporting `OptimizedCache`, `ArrayBufferPool`, `StringProcessor`, `LazyLoader`, `Debouncer`, `PerformanceMonitor`, two cache-value interfaces, a `globalOptimizations` singleton, and `initializeOptimizations` / `cleanupOptimizations` helpers — none of it reachable.

## Verification that it is dormant

- Every exported symbol searched by name repo-wide: only self-references inside the file. The one near-miss, `BuildPerformanceMonitor` in `docs/scripts/build-performance.ts`, is a different symbol in an unrelated file.
- Dynamic `import(` / `require(` searched across `apps/moo-dang`: 28 hits, none referencing this module.
- `apps/moo-dang/src/utils/index.ts` re-exports `accessibility-keyboard`, `output-formatting`, `scrollback-manager`, and `terminal-keys` only. The app's sole `export *` is in `src/components/index.ts`, a different directory.
- No config, build, or workflow references.
- No test file existed for it.

The only mention anywhere is `.ai/audit/audit-phase2-analysis.md`, an archived planning document.

## Why delete rather than keep

Beyond being unreachable, an architectural review flagged a likely defect in `OptimizedCache`'s eviction scoring around lines 97-102: increasing age raises an entry's score, but the ascending sort evicts the lowest score — so it appears to evict newer entries rather than older ones. Nobody can hit it, because nothing calls it.

That matters for the decision. This is not working code waiting for a consumer; it is unexercised code with at least one suspected bug in its core policy. Reviving it later should mean rewriting it against real requirements, not trusting six-hundred lines that have never run.

Keeping it also has a recurring cost. Six of the twelve classes flagged by the convention audit in #1937 live in this file, so every nightly pass re-reports them.

Git history retains it if it is ever wanted. [description truncated to fit budget]
title: chore(moo-dang): remove dormant performance-optimizations module
